newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs surge in Tokyo but 124.00 barrier still holds.
newsitem.headline: JGBs surge in Tokyo but 124.00 barrier still holds.

text.p: The benchmark September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract surged to end Friday morning Tokyo trade sharply higher, buoyed by an array of factors from weaker-than-expected Tokyo stocks to the market's successful absorption of a large volume of corporate straight bonds issued recently, traders said.
But resistance at 124.00 was holding, and traders said it would be difficult to go above this without investor buying, with any such rises being quickly met by sales.
Key September ended the morning at 123.83, up a whopping 0.37 from Thursday's close, with turnover of 27,373 contracts.
Prior to the start of trade, the market had been extremely nervous about possible gains in Tokyo stocks after the Dow set a fresh record high for the fifth straight day.

But aside from an initial jump to a new high for the calendar year just after the opening, which pushed bonds to their day's low of 123.51, trade was unimpressive, with the Nikkei finally ending the morning up by 80.30 at 20,644.76.

While traders acknowledged that this had indeed cleared the way for bonds to rise, they said a shift to positive sentiment after aggressive short-covering lifted September in overnight trade also played an important role.

This feeling was augmented by signs that the market is managing to successfully absorb the first part of about 300 to 400 billion yen worth of corporate straight bonds to be launched starting this week and ending at the end of next week.
Among these are the 30 billion yen of straight bonds launched by Mitsubishi Estate Co Ltd on Wednesday, with Fujitsu Ltd expected to launch 100 billion yen worth of bonds next week.
The market had been concerned that this flood of fresh issues could weigh the market down, but a city bank trader said sales appear to be proceeding briskly.

Additional support came from the lingering impact of a Thursday comment by senior Ministry of Finance official Eisuke Sakakibara that Japan's interest rates are unlikely to rise anytime soon, a trust bank trader said.

But some in the market worry that sharp growth in Japan's first quarter gross domestic product (GDP), due out at 0630 GMT today, could perhaps revive speculation about higher interest rates. Economists polled by Reuters said on average they expect real GDP for the period to have grown 1.1 percent from the previous quarter, which registered a growth rate of 1.0 percent. Forecasts ranged from 0.3 percent to 1.6 percent.
Morning trade in futures was mainly powered by short-covering led by traders, although some traders said investor buying of the medium-term zone was also bolstering the long end.
Cash bonds were also strong. The yield on the benchmark 10-year 182nd cash bond stood at 2.400 at 0238 GMT against 2.430 percent at Thursday's Tokyo close.
